mappingNotes: Source inventory of current E:/openim checkout; deployment, current-group lookup and write contracts were provided by the user. Source review and local tests do not establish live backend deployment or real traffic.

Two destinations are intentional: business endpoints retain /api/v1 contract paths and use SangongApiConfig; current-group GET/POST/PUT use the current Chat base plus literal /sangong/api/v1 paths, bypassing Sangong business base/prefix/tenant overrides.
SangongGameHttp uses https://sangong.invalid only as an intercepted Dio placeholder, not a production destination.

All Sangong-specific requests require current account Sangong privilege. Current-group existence lookup does not require canConfigure/canManage, so all-false capabilities do not imply an absent tenant. Current-group creation additionally requires native group owner/admin and a matching current game group; existing-tenant update is controlled by current canConfigure in the page and server authorization, not inferred from SDK admin.

Current gameType=1 management requires account privilege, an active configured current-group point-lookup result, aggregate canManage and a verified logical binding; it does not require ex.groupFeatures or its legacy enabled/manageEntry switches. Ordinary/legacy admin/settings routes retain enabled/manageEntry/canManage. agent/me routes retain enabled/agentEntry/canOpenAgent; member-daily and transfers additionally require rebateHistoryEntry/canViewRebateHistory.

Ordinary business HTTP/SSE X-Tenant-Id prefers the verified logical tenantId over SANGONG_TENANT_ID. The default deployment fallback is @z8hFfDvVQP0x; it grants neither group capability nor verified binding.

Legacy business extraSkipTenant routes (default my-config, default members, tenant list and agent entry-context) bypass only the logical-binding prerequisite: with a nonempty configured fallback they send that fallback even if a logical tenant exists; with empty SANGONG_TENANT_ID they omit X-Tenant-Id. Current-group Chat GET/POST/PUT always omit the tenant header.

Every Sangong-specific request and SSE connection uses the current Chat chatToken as Authorization: Bearer, JSON content type and fresh operationID. The three shared privilege/capability/identity dependencies retain their original Chat token-header behavior. SSE also sends Accept: text/event-stream.

Only HTTP 404 plus exact serverCode TENANT_NOT_FOUND means current-group notFound. Only HTTP 403 plus exact TENANT_ACCESS_DENIED means accessDenied and contact-the-configurer guidance. active:false is disabled; 401, other privilege/permission 403, generic 404, 503, network and format errors do not become absent tenants.

Current-group successful DTO parsing requires a native boolean active and matching explicit tenant IDs; current-game explicit imGroupGameId must match the current group. Successful point queries may fill omitted IDs with the requested ID. Explicit agent tenant lookup may retain a different betting group. Missing role/permission fields stay empty/false, and no query result grants capabilities.

Current-group POST201 confirms only explicit ok:true, active:true and a complete matching game/bot configuration. PUT200 uses complete matching configuration and boolean active, without requiring configured/canEditConfig. Incomplete or rejected successful-status write bodies report UNKNOWN_RESULT; known HTTP/backend errors remain errors, and stale account/API/group/privilege results are discarded.

GET my-config reads the account default tenant; PUT my-config changes that default. Neither determines current-chat-group registration. The default configuration page and strict configured parser remain, but current-group pages use the point lookup/write adapter and do not expose default my-config/members.

Privileged gameType=1 chats query current-game registration independently of management capabilities. Ordinary groups and nonprivileged accounts do not add this lookup. Agent-only groups retain their capability/entry-context aggregate tenantID instead of treating the agent groupID as a missing game tenant.

callStatus active means a current application method is referenced, not captured traffic. Conditional current/legacy branches retain their reasons; reserved means no application caller found, not that the backend lacks the endpoint.

60 distinct method+path templates: 49 active (including three current-group tenant methods and two betting fallback paths), 11 reserved. There are 59 ordinary HTTP routes and one SSE GET route. Three shared dependencies and seven reference-only methods are counted separately.

SSE bypasses the SangongGameHttp Dio adapter but shares requestPath/requestHeaders, verified-tenant preference and Bearer authentication. Current-group point methods independently guard the captured Chat session/API/base and account privilege revision.

Ordinary business responses preserve the proxy envelope and reject business errors or ok=false before endpoint parsing. Point-lookup states preserve the complete success raw envelope; GroupFeatureException preserves actual HTTP statusCode and backend serverCode while generic shared 404/501 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE behavior remains.
Parameter types and required fields describe current serialization, UI guards and the explicit user contract. Optional response properties still require a complete server schema where not supplied.
Settings save/updateMaxBet share PUT settings; assignBanker/setDoorCount share POST banker/setup. Wrapper methods do not introduce additional routes.
GitNexus registry has no index for this E:/openim checkout; source inventory was checked locally rather than using another checkout graph.

configuration.fullVersionBaseRule: For bases ending /api/v1, ignore SANGONG_API_PATH_PREFIX and strip exactly one leading /api/v1 from endpoint paths.
configuration.rootBaseRule: For bases not ending /api/v1, append normalized SANGONG_API_PATH_PREFIX and the complete endpoint /api/v1 path.
configuration.emptyBaseBehavior: Explicit empty SANGONG_API_BASE_URL uses current Config.appAuthUrl.
configuration.emptyTenantBehavior: Ordinary business requests use the verified logical tenant; legacy extraSkipTenant discovery/default routes omit the header. Current-group Chat methods always omit it.
configuration.sharedDependenciesBehavior: The three shared Chat dependencies keep the current Chat base and token header. Sangong-specific current-group tenant methods also use Chat but explicitly opt into Bearer and omit X-Tenant-Id.
